text:
marta: Quick check — ran multi-GPU inference benchmarks on PCIe and SXM nodes across us-west and eu-central. SXM shows higher throughput but p95/p99 latency spikes on synchronized multi-GPU runs in eu-central. Anyone seen NUMA/cpu-affinity or NVLink mismatches cause this?

sam: Can you paste the perf summary and the node types? NVLink topology differences across regions is a common gotcha. :thinking:

marta: Summary (very condensed):
```
model: t6-7b-8k, batch=1 streams=16
us-west-pcie (4xA10): throughput=580 req/s, p95=48ms, p99=82ms
eu-central-pcie (4xA10): throughput=520 req/s, p95=50ms, p99=120ms
sxm (4xH100): throughput=980 req/s, p95=32ms, p99=60ms
note: sync KV cache + cross-GPU attention enabled
```
Observations: SXM better overall but eu-central PCIe has a long p99 tail that only shows up under 4-GPU runs.

josh: Two quick checks: 1) confirm NVLink peer access with `nvidia-smi topo -m` 2) try pinning the process to the same NUMA node as the GPUs. Example: 
```
# check nvlink
nvidia-smi topo -m
# pin CPU/memory to NUMA node 1 and bind GPUs 0,1
numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1 python serve.py --gpus=0,1
```
Also set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to map logical ids consistently.

kris: From similar experiments: if GPUs are across different PCIe root complexes (cross-socket), cross-GPU collectives pay a big latency tax. We saw ~15-25% worse p99 if not pinned. Quick numbers from our last run:
- PCIe (no pin): p99=118ms
- PCIe (numa pin + NVLink enforced): p99=86ms
So pinning matter. Also try switching kernel selection for large matmuls — in our runtime we fell back to `fast_gemm_v1` which has worse latency in some shapes. For H100/SXM you want `fast_gemm_v2` / fused-kernel enabled.

marta: Helpful — I'll rerun with numactl and force NVLink-aware routing. Any suggested runtime env flags?

josh: You can toggle the runtime routing with envs we have in staging: `REDWOOD_FORCE_NVLINK=1` and to avoid fallback to pci paths `REDWOOD_DISABLE_PCI_FALLBACK=1` (use cautiously). Also `REDWOOD_NUMA_AWARE=1` will enable CPU->GPU affinity heuristics.

sam: Also check kernel/drivers across regions — mismatched CUDA driver (e.g., 12.x vs 12.y) or different OFED version sometimes disables peer access silently. `nvidia-smi topo -m` will show `PX`/`PHB` vs `NV` links. If you see lots of PHB/PCIe hops, expect higher tail.

kris: One more micro-tip: for batched decoding use asynchronous overlap of IO + compute and avoid global synchronizations between GPUs on the hot path. That reduced p99 significantly for us. :rocket:

bench-bot: CI run linked: https://ci.redwood.internal/runs/bench/1742539845 — gpu-topo-check + perf artifacts uploaded. :white_check_mark:

marta: Perfect. I'll re-run eu-central with numactl mapping + REDWOOD_FORCE_NVLINK=1, capture nvlink topology and lspci output, and upload results to the model-onboarding doc so we have a region-specific checklist. Will post summary once done. Thanks all! :+1:
